chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-'Abdi, from al-A'mash, from 'Abaya ibn Rib'i, from 'Abdallah ibn 'Abbas, from his father. He said:

Abu Talib said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): O nephew! Did God send you? He said: Yes. He said: Then show me a sign. He said: Call to that tree for me. So he called it, and it came forward until it prostrated before him. Then it went away. So Abu Talib said: I bear witness that you are truthful. O Ali, pray behind your cousin.

key_terms.آيَة: A divine sign or miracle, proof of prophethood; used in the Quran to indicate both Quranic verses and miraculous proofs
key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness — the formula of testimony (shahada), echoing the declaration of faith
key_terms.جَنَاح: Literally 'wing/flank' — here used idiomatically meaning 'alongside' or 'behind', indicating following in prayer

ai.seo_question: Did Abu Talib believe in the Prophet? What miracle witnessed by Abu Talib is recorded in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration records the moment Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle and protector, witnessed a miraculous sign — a tree prostrating before the Prophet at his command — which prompted Abu Talib to declare his belief in the Prophet's truthfulness. The account concludes with Abu Talib instructing his son Ali to pray behind the Prophet, an act understood in the Shia tradition as Abu Talib's implicit affirmation of Islam. The transmission chain spans the Prophet's uncle 'Abbas through the scholar Ibn 'Abbas, linking back to this intimate family event.
